commands.help: requests, tasks and what waits for you
where the work stands and what happened (since: 7d, <n>d or YYYY-MM-DD)

what waits for you; with an id, that decision whole (the MCP mode and a messaging reader without the group ask-mail do not see the current text of an event a calendar card shows, nor the addresses, the subject, the text and the attachment names of an e-mail card)

answer a pending decision; the answer to a question may come back with a proposal (instruction_proposal) to add your own line to the project's instructions, which is added only by instructions-add, from the terminal or the page
release a delivery (it stays a draft)

approve a plan or an acceptance (a plan: --go-ahead <task key>, repeated, drops that task's derived waits); an effect is approved with its hash, in the terminal, on the page, or on a messaging app the project grants that effect's word (from a card that carried the whole text)
reject a plan, an acceptance or an effect
make a failed or blocked task ready again
cancel a request at any moment, even while a task of it runs: the run is ended and returns nothing, what it used so far is spent
stop one running task: its run is ended and returns nothing, the task is blocked, and retry resumes it

answer a question from the text of the project's sources, with the quotes it rests on and the sources and versions read: one run of the answer skill, no plan to approve; the sources are chosen by code (@<id> to name them), the answer goes only to the shell or chat that asked; never the MCP mode, and on a messaging app only for a sender whose profile lists the group ask

the files people sent through a messaging app (from a messaging app, only the ones you sent): those held for your answer (name, kind, size, the source each would become, when it expires), the latest decisions, the day's count and the limits; a held file is in the data folder, never in a run, a prompt or the sources folder
start a new request, whatever is open (--after <id> before the text: run it after that request)
